summary: The article, dated September 17, 2023, describes how small businesses are struggling to find and keep workers as millennials and Gen Z favor flexibility, purpose and the gig economy. It offers strategies drawn from several experts: flexible job descriptions, in-person networking, social media recruiting, training programs, personalized benefits and a values-driven brand. Julianne Baxter and Rebecca Torres are cited as local owners dealing with these pressures.
one_line: Small businesses are adapting hiring to millennial and Gen Z expectations through flexibility, networking, social media, training, personalized benefits and branding.
key_facts: Julianne Baxter owns Baxter's Bakery in downtown Springfield and has run the family business for a decade.
Baxter says small businesses are "competing with the freedom and flexibility that the gig economy offers, especially to younger workers."
Craig Simon, an HR consultant in Minneapolis, says millennials and Gen Z see a job as part of their identity and life plan, not just a paycheck.
Simon recommends flexible work arrangements, co-working space memberships, wellness programs, financial planning assistance and continued learning opportunities.
Rebecca Torres, a local boutique owner, found her star employee at a chamber of commerce networking event on November 5, 2023.
In-person networking is gaining traction among small businesses and requires building relationships long before a hiring need arises.
Martha Jensen, a social media strategist working with small businesses in the greater Seattle area, advocates using Instagram and TikTok to show company culture.
Zachary Li, founder of a coding bootcamp, says businesses offering training, especially in digital and tech, become attractors for talent.
Training and development aids retention because employees feel valued and see a path forward within the company.
Nontraditional benefits suggested include remote work days, pet-friendly offices and partnerships with local businesses for employee discounts.
Jeffrey Tan, a small business advisor in Atlanta, calls the one-size-fits-all benefits package outdated and says personalized perks can set a business apart.
Small business owners should clearly communicate mission and values in every job posting, including ethical stances, sustainability and community involvement.
